critique.root_cause: This is a fundamental pipeline failure, not a tuning issue. Cova has either (1) completely ignored the structural preservation mask/inpainting strategy, (2) not implemented depth-aware generation that locks architectural elements, (3) over-weighted the style prompt so heavily that it overrode structural conditioning, or (4) is using a pure text-to-image generation rather than image-to-image with proper structural guidance. The result is a beautiful render of a DIFFERENT room. This would be like asking for a kitchen remodel and getting a bathroom - technically well-executed but completely wrong. The system appears to be treating this as 'generate a Japandi bedroom' rather than 'redesign THIS SPECIFIC bedroom in Japandi style.' This is a showstopper failure that makes the tool unusable for its intended purpose, regardless of how good the photorealism is.
specific_fixes: PRIORITY 1: Implement structural preservation pipeline - use ControlNet depth map + edge detection to lock room geometry before any style application

PRIORITY 2: Create non-negotiable preservation masks for: walls (color must match original), ceiling fixtures (position + type locked), windows (preserve blinds/curtains from original), floor material (carpet vs hardwood must match)
PRIORITY 3: Add LoRA or embedding for personal elements - 'DAKSH' letters should be detected via OCR and re-injected at exact coordinates post-generation
PRIORITY 4: Implement camera pose locking - extract camera parameters from original and enforce identical viewpoint in generation
PRIORITY 5: Use two-stage generation: Stage 1 = remove existing furniture only (inpaint with structural context), Stage 2 = add new furniture with style conditioning but preserve Stage 1 structure
PRIORITY 6: Reduce style prompt weight/CFG scale - currently style is dominating over structural conditioning
PRIORITY 7: Add validation layer - detect if major structural elements (wall color, ceiling type, floor material) changed >threshold, auto-reject generation
PRIORITY 8: Implement regional prompting - separate prompts for 'preserve wall as blue-gray' vs 'add Japandi furniture'
PRIORITY 9: Use original image at higher strength in img2img (currently appears to be <0.3 denoise, needs to be ~0.6-0.7 to maintain structure)
PRIORITY 10: Add explicit negative prompts: 'white walls, hardwood floor, cove ceiling, curtains, different room'
